nightdash-bot: [ALERT] Overnight perf dashboard: 99th latency for small-gen saw a 2.3x jump between 03:00-04:30 UTC. metric: runtime.kernel_latency.p99

alice: seeing it too on the canary graphs, tail drift starts ~03:05. Noticable on 1-2k token requests.

ben: CI perf job also failed ~03:10 with increased kernel selection time in the trace. cc @carol @dima

carol: linking the CI trace: https://ci.internal/runs/98234/trace  — kernel selector shows extra 8ms on average for batch join.

alice: we rolled merge 6f2c8 into main at 02:45. suspecting kernel scheduling heuristic change in that PR.

dima: running quick bisect locally between main@pre-merge and main@post-merge. grabbing perf profile.

ben: if it's kernel selection, maybe the epsilon threshold in selector got tightened, causing more handoffs. that would show as increased KV lookups.

nightdash-bot: added alert annotation: suspected-change=kernel-selector; affected-pools=gpu-dedicated-1

carol: perf profile (sampling, 10s window):
```
# sample hot stacks
runtime::select_kernel 45%
runtime::kv_cache::lookup 12%
runtime::batcher::join 25%
other 18%
```

alice: interesting - select_kernel dominating. can we get the selector decision logs for the time window? maybe a parameter flip causing different candidate ordering.

dima: pulled selector logs from canary: lots of retries where primary kernel reported incompatible sequence length and we fall back to slower kernel. looks like primary kernel handshake started failing on ~3% of requests.

ben: handshake failures -> that points to the merge that adjusted kernel capability matching (PR #4217).

carol: quick grep in 6f2c8 shows this change: `if min_seq >= req_len { prefer_primary = true }` replaced with `if min_seq > req_len { prefer_primary = true }` — off-by-one.

alice: that would make previously eligible kernels be considered incompatible for equal-length requests. tiny condition change, big perf hit.

eva: can we hotfix by reverting the one-line change and redeploy? Or add a guard to treat equality as compatible while we test.

dima: I pushed a revert branch (revert/kernel-compat-offbyone) and started a canary rollout to a single pool. deploy id: deploy-1759005601

nightdash-bot: deploy event: deploy-1759005601 started -> canary @ gpu-dedicated-1

ben: canary metrics already showing improvement at 03:40 — p99 back down ~1.05x baseline.

carol: running CI perf job against revert branch. if green we can roll forward revert to main.

alice: also add a regression test for equal-length matching to avoid future slips. small unit test plus an e2e perf micro-benchmark.

eva: noted, I'll open a quickissue: https://go/redwood/issue/INF-2123 with test plan.

dima: CI perf job passed on revert at 03:58. patch ready: revert PR #4229.

ben: scheduling release freeze lift once revert is merged and main canaries look stable for 1hr.

alice: thanks for quick bisect everyone. postmortem: small conditional change caused large selector divergence -> increased fallbacks to slower kernels -> tail latency surge during low-traffic overnight window.

nightdash-bot: Alert resolved (auto) after canary improvement. root_cause_tag=selector-off-by-one; fix=revert-PR-4229; mitigation=added test+monitoring.

carol: follow-ups: (1) add equality test to kernel capability matcher, (2) alert to include kernel fallback count as first-class metric, (3) add canary health check to fail rollouts if fallback_rate > 0.5%. I'll own 1&3.

alice: created the postmortem stub in confluence: https://confluence/internal/infra/INF-2123-postmortem — fill in timelines and mitigation notes.

eva: thumbs up. closing thread once revert merged to main and nightly verifies stable for 2 cycles. :thumbsup:
